hypotheses.confidence_note: Conditional two-second local prototype, not a verified trajectory or world-safety claim. Ego starts at the supplied 5.4273 m/s; the 3 m/s preference requests deceleration while beginning the visible left bend. The convex road is a conservative local pavement approximation, not the entire bend or parking lot. Monocular positions, road boundaries and residuals are model estimates. Other visible parked lot vehicles, the rear-right Nissan and rear-left truck are outside the modeled forward pavement patch and are explicitly assumed not to enter it; hidden pedestrians, vehicle pull-outs and new entrants are excluded conditions, not observations of absence. The nearby white hatch is retained despite its asynchronous side-camera evidence. No optimizer, dynamics verifier or prefix simulator was available in this response.

premises.statement: The modeled driving domain is only this finite continuous pavement patch, including the current ego footprint and an approximately eight-to-nine-meter forward route beginning the left bend. Adopt no new unobserved entrant into this patch over two seconds. Other visible parking-lot vehicles, rear-right Nissan and rear-left truck remain in their current parking areas outside this patch; no hidden pedestrian emerges. These are falsifiable exclusions, not assertions about the whole scene. Declared neighboring actors retain their explicit body envelopes even where those envelopes lie outside this domain.

Assume ordinary passenger-car dimensions as natively declared and approximately level, continuous pavement over the short local patch. Estimate depth and lateral placement from apparent vehicle dimensions, perspective, visible wheel/contact neighborhoods and curb edges using supplied camera axes; calibration alone does not establish metric depth. The blue sedan's 4.6 m length and 1.8 m width are conditional size priors. The latest front view shows the inner curb rising leftward and the outer parking curb converging ahead; side/rear views support the near-ego continuation. The road polygon clips the observed curved patch to a convex local subset; its 0.4 m residual represents noncalibrated boundary error. These scale and pavement assumptions also apply at the white hatch's capture, 0.042121 seconds before reference.

The two reference-visible cars appear parked against the far-side curb/parking area. Adopt fixed body pose for two seconds. Reasonable adverse mode within the adopted parked condition permits at most 0.30 m translation in any direction with unchanged yaw; it excludes an active pull-out. Each adverse rectangular source expands the nominal full oriented-body bounding box by at least that translation range. Source residuals represent additional model geometry error, not body dimensions.

The front-right image shows the white hatch fully within a parking bay, with no visible pull-out indication. Conditional on remaining parked, bound absolute center speed by 0.15 m/s and keep yaw at its estimated 2.1 rad from its actual capture through the two-second horizon. The 0.042121 s capture-to-reference displacement is at most 0.006319 m, conservatively bounded by 0.007 m. Adopt zero motion; adverse mode permits up to 0.30 m future displacement in any direction. The evidence position is expressed in fixed reference axes using supplied ego history. Alignment residual 0.4 m additionally covers imperfect visual pose and compensation; future source residual is separate.

anchors.rationale: The individually visible blue-gray four-door sedan has a conventional compact/midsize body. A 4.6 m body length is an assumed class-size prior, not a measured specification.
Assumed ordinary sedan body width, matching this actor's native body geometry and excluding mirrors.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: In the reference front image the blue-gray sedan occupies approximately u=950..1265 and its lower wheel/body contact neighborhood is around v=590..605. Its oblique, largely side-visible 4.6 m assumed body supports an order-15-to-20-meter range; the native estimate is center [17,-4.1] with yaw 2.6 rad. Its image displacement right of the principal point supports negative Y. Applying this approximate scale to visible curbs and pavement perspective gives a roughly seven-meter near-field paved width that turns left and narrows in fixed-reference X. The road is clipped at X=12 m rather than extrapolated through the full bend. The distant gray hatch and side-visible white hatch are estimated consistently with ordinary car-size priors. None of these estimates is calibrated ground-plane reconstruction.
